Seminar Title:

Electrocaloric effect and energy storage studies of lead-free BST-based ferroelectric systems

Seminar Type:

Pawan Kumar

Abstract:

Lead-free ferroelectric ceramics have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation solid-state cooling and energy storage devices due to their environmental compatibility and multifunctional behavior. In this work, a sequential compositional strategy is adopted in BaTiO₃ (BT)-based ceramics, where strontium substitution is first used to tune the phase transition toward near-room temperature, followed by tin incorporation to further optimize polarization dynamics and induce relaxor behavior. High-energy ball milling enables the formation of homogeneous, fine-grained ceramics with enhanced densification and controlled microstructure. Structural analysis confirmed the stabilization of a ferroelectric phase, supported by Raman studies. The Sr-doped BT system exhibited a diffuse phase transition, while Sn doping induced relaxor-like characteristics, ensuring a stable dielectric response over a broad temperature range. Consequently, enhanced energy storage performance with improved efficiency and reduced hysteresis loss is achieved, along with slimmer polarization loops under thermal variation. Simultaneously, a significant electrocaloric response near ambient conditions highlights strong polarization-entropy coupling, demonstrating the potential of this approach for multifunctional and sustainable device applications.
